From the initial torus to an outflow

The black hole and magnetohydrodynamics are coupled through a fixed Kerr metric. Accretion carries magnetic flux toward the horizon; the polar funnel emerges from the solution.

The volume is reconstructed by revolving an axisymmetric solution. This does not represent three-dimensional turbulence. Color and opacity visualize the data; they do not predict an observed image.

PHYSICS / NUMERICS / EVIDENCE

Now solving the equations
in the Kerr metric.

The main sequence was produced by a separate run of iharm2d_v4. The viewer replays saved solutions; it does not rerun the simulation in the browser. Rendering does not prescribe the dynamics.

∇μ(ρuμ) = 0
∇μ Tμν = 0
∇μ *Fμν = 0
Tμν = (ρ + u + p + b²)uμuν + (p + b²/2)gμν − bμbν

Initial state

Fishbone–Moncrief torus: r_in = 6, r_max = 12, a* = 0.9375. The initial poloidal loop is specified by Aφ ∝ max(ρ/ρ_max − 0.2, 0). The ratio of the maximum gas pressure to the maximum magnetic pressure is 100; this does not require β = 100 at every point. Internal energy is perturbed by the pseudorandom factor 1 + 0.04(ξ−0.5), with seed = 1. γad = 1.333333. No external magnetic energy is injected.

Domain and method

96 × 96 cells in FMKS coordinates, r ∈ [1.0822, 50] GM/c²; the inner boundary lies inside the horizon. WENO reconstruction, constrained transport for the magnetic field, CFL = 0.7. Standard code boundary conditions: radial outflow with boundary inflow disabled, and polar conditions on the axis. Source: iharm2d_v4, commit ea28799b56e88dfcdecccb2d7bdcf87037d97ef4. The core solver was not modified; only the problem parameters were changed.

Reading the diagnostics

Ṁ = −∫ρu¹√−g dx²dφ. P_EM = −∫T¹_t,EM√−g dx²dφ. The integration surface passes through the cell center nearest the horizon, not the exact horizon. Positive P_EM denotes an outward electromagnetic flux of Killing energy; it is not the total jet efficiency. All fluxes use the code normalization ρ_max(t=0) = 1; the black-hole mass and physical accretion rate are unspecified.

*Γ is the maximum Lorentz factor relative to the normal observer, restricted to cells with 5 < r < 20, u¹ > 0 and σ = b²/ρ > 1. This diagnostic mask does not prove that all selected gas will reach infinity. The speed shown in the slice is √(1−Γ⁻²) where u¹ > 0, and zero where u¹ ≤ 0.

Floors and numerical reliability

Artificial floors maintain density and internal energy in nearly evacuated regions; the code caps magnetization at approximately b²/ρ = 100. This affects jet mass loading and Γ. Failed conserved-to-primitive inversions are handled by the standard code repair procedure. Inversion and floor flags are retained in the diagnostics. Small div B and accurate four-velocity normalization do not establish convergence. MRI and three-dimensional instabilities are not fully resolved; no convergence study has been performed. A quasi-steady state is not assumed.

Rendering

The 2D volume is reconstructed by revolving an axisymmetric slice; the 3D mode uses the computed three-dimensional fields. An illustrative emission function makes the dense torus and magnetic outflow visible. Color ranges are fixed. The spatial embedding is R = r sinθ, z = r cosθ, not a representation of proper spatial distances. The black circle or sphere marks the coordinate horizon radius, not an optical shadow. Lensing, Doppler boosting, absorption and spectra are not calculated.

Field lines are integrated using the computed coordinate magnetic field, transformed to the displayed spatial coordinates, then overlaid without occlusion. Their number and seed locations are illustrative choices. Fields are interpolated onto a rendering grid; interpolation does not increase simulation resolution.

Three-dimensional run

The reproducibility bundle records the parameters and actual duration of the 3D run.

Reproducibility

The archive contains source code and licenses, configuration, selected original ASCII and binary dumps compressed with gzip, analysis, diagnostics and rerun scripts. A proposed 3D calculation is not a completed run. Higher resolution, extended 3D evolution, convergence testing and radiative transfer remain separate stages.
